hook.line: Interviewer's question: will AI be smarter than all humans? He says he believes it will.
hook.visual: Tight close-up of a guest in glasses, serif title 'Will AI be smarter than all humans?' builds line by line at left, small subtitles at bottom.

beats.what: Close-up of the guest as the question is read; serif title appears line by line.
Guest affirms AI will reach that level.
Cut to the interviewer asking whether he worries about the unknowns.
Back on the guest; name lower third appears in red with his title.
Lists the risks: economic impact, misuse, losing control of the model.
Tighter angle as he lands on 'call it as you see it, be willing to be wrong'.

why_it_works: A big yes/no question on screen from frame one frames the clip as a debate the viewer has an opinion on (245 comments).
Very tight close-ups (face fills about half the frame height) make a calm answer feel intimate and serious.
A single reverse shot of the interviewer at 8.2 s is the only cut needed to reset attention before the answer.
Clip ends on a quotable line ('be willing to be wrong sometimes').
weaknesses: No music, no motion events and only 5 cuts in 36 s: it relies entirely on the speaker's authority.
Subtitles are small and all text sits outside the safe area.
No call to action or next step.
for_robert: Open with his question as a big on-screen title that builds line by line while he answers, so the frame poses a debate before he says a word.
